problem: A rectangular cow pasture is enclosed on three sides by a fence and the fourth side is part of the side of a barn that is $400$ feet long. The fence costs $\$5$ per foot, and $\$1,\!200$ altogether. To the nearest foot, find the length of the side parallel to the barn that will maximize the area of the pasture.
solution_to_review: Let the sides perpendicular to the barn be of length $x$. Notice that there are a total of $1200/5=200$ feet of fencing. Therefore, the side parallel to the barn has length $200-2x$, so the area to be maximized is $200x-2x^2+100$. Completing the square results in $-2(x-50)^2+720$, which is maximized when $x=50$. Therefore, the side parallel to the barn has length $200-2(50)=\boxed{100}$ feet.
